A list that shows messages starred in a community space.
A system that enables such a list.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English sterbord, stere-bourd, stere-burd, from Old English stēorbord, from Proto-West Germanic *steurubord, equivalent to steer + board (“side (of a ship)”), referring to ancient ships with the steering oar set to the right (to accommodate right-handed crew). Ships had to dock on their left (port) side because the steering oar on the right would get in the way, which is how the left became known as the port side.

senses.definition: to turn the wheel or steer a vessel toward the right side

examples.en: The captain ordered the crew to starboard.

examples.en: Undeterred by the heavy rain, the athletes continued running.

examples.en: The young candidate hoped to unseat the current mayor.

senses.vi: cách chức; lật đổ; làm mất ghế

thesaurus.definition: remove from political office
dislodge from one's seat, as from a horse

vi_block: Đẩy ra khỏi chỗ ngồi; làm ng (người cưỡi ngựa).
Cách chức, làm mất ghế (nghị sĩ).
Coi là vô hiệu, thủ tiêu.

examples: The frightened horse reared up and unseated its rider.
I was unseated from my bike after hitting an unexpected pothole.
wiktionary.gloss: To dislodge or remove (someone) from a seat, especially on horseback.

examples: After having lost her seat to a Tory, she succeeded in unseating him in the next general election.
India has recently unseated China as the world’s most populous country.
wiktionary.gloss: To remove (someone) from an office or position, especially a political one; to dethrone.

examples: The Michelson-Morley experiment prompted scientists to unseat their belief in the luminiferous aether.
Printed newspapers are gradually being unseated by digital publications.
wiktionary.gloss: To cause (something) to be removed or replaced in its role; to displace, to overturn.

examples: The Matrix (1999) utterly unseated audiences around the world with its mind-blowing plot twist.
I was somewhat unseated by the strange noises outside my window.
wiktionary.gloss: To upset the composure of (someone); to astound, to shock, to unsettle.

examples: We replaced the screws, since the old ones unseated too easily.
wiktionary.gloss: To come off or out of a seat.

thesaurus.definition: a home appliance for washing clothes and linens automatically

examples: She put all the dirty clothes in the washing machine.
wiktionary.gloss: A machine, usually automatic, that washes clothes, etc.

examples: We are waiting with bated breath for the release of the new version.
